title: Limit on Open Retail Installment Contracts per Borrower
content:
**Rule.** A borrower may hold several Retail Installment Contracts, but never more than **2** contracts at the same time whose status is pending funding, active or repossessed. Contracts that are paid off, liquidated, charged off or unwound do not count toward the limit.

A purchase that would exceed the limit is declined at booking, and no contract is booked.

The basis on which a second open contract is admitted, and how open contracts combine, is governed by the company's rule on combined exposure across a borrower's open contracts.

| Borrower already holds (counting statuses pending funding, active, repossessed) | New purchase |
|---|---|
| no counting contract | within the limit |
| 1 counting contract | within the limit of 2 |
| 2 counting contracts | declined at booking; no contract is booked |

**Hypothetical case.** A borrower holds one active contract and one paid-off contract. Only the active contract counts, so a new purchase would bring the count to 2, which is within the limit. Had the earlier contract instead been repossessed, both would count and the new purchase would be declined.
